**The market's 100% concentration on 92-93°F reflects the official high temperature of 93°F recorded at Denver International Airport on August 12, 2026, per National Weather Service climatological data.** 

This outcome aligns with NWS point forecasts and ensemble model consensus issued in the days prior, which projected highs in the low-to-mid 90s under partly sunny skies with limited afternoon thunderstorm activity. The result fits within broader August 2026 conditions that followed early-month extremes near 102°F but moderated toward seasonal norms (climatological average high ~88°F). Trader positioning converged rapidly as observational data and short-range models locked in the narrow range, leaving negligible implied probability for bins outside 92-95°F.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the King Abdulaziz International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 13 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the King Abdulaziz International Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/sa/jeddah/OEJN.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: August's peak heat season in Jeddah, combined with above-average temperature forecasts from models projecting daily highs of 38–41°C or more, drives the 71.5% market-implied probability for a 41°C or higher peak on August 13. Coastal Red Sea humidity and typical August climatology, with historical averages near 38°C but recent regional outlooks showing 1–2°C anomalies across Saudi Arabia, support elevated readings. Official monitoring indicates minimal cooling influences like cloud cover or wind shifts in current guidance, though forecast uncertainty remains due to potential model revisions or localized sea breezes. Traders weigh these factors against historical extremes exceeding 43°C in similar conditions.

Persistent clear to partly cloudy conditions favor strong solar heating, yet isolated afternoon thunderstorms—already indicated in extended forecasts—could trim peak temperatures by 1–2°C through increased cloud cover and brief evaporative cooling. Historical mid-August analogs show daily maxima averaging 32–34°C but frequently reaching 36–38°C during heat episodes, with variability driven mainly by the exact timing and coverage of convective activity. Updated model runs over the next 48 hours will likely resolve whether conditions stay hot and dry enough for 37°C or trend slightly cooler.
